newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank of China to expand loans in 1997 - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China to expand loans in 1997 - newspaper.

text.p: The state-owned Bank of China will boost services in 1997 and expand loans to meet competition expected from the entry of foreign banks into the domestic yuan currency business, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

"The competition posts both challenges and motivation for us," the newspaper quoted bank president Wang Xuebing as saying at a meeting of officials of nationwide branches of the state-owned commercial bank on Monday.

"The banks are not only our rivals but also our examples and cooperative partners," he said, referring to the decision to allow four overseas banks based in Shanghai's Pudong New Area to conduct yuan business.
The Bank of China would promote international settlement business and foreign exchange transactions, he said.
The bank aimed to expand total assets by 8.0 percent in 1997 from nearly 1.8199 trillion yuan in 1996, he said.

It plans to increase local currency deposits by 88 billion yuan, from a total of 486.4 billion yuan in 1996 and to boost foreign currency deposits by $1.5 billion from $29.3 billion as of the end of last year, he said.
The bank planned to increase its loans by 50 million yuan ($6.0 million), from domestic loans outstanding of 475.0 billion yuan at the end of last year, he said.
The bank would initiate mortgage loans for residential housing, Wang said.
The Bank of China reported after-tax profits of 8.2 billion yuan on income of 206.7 billion yuan from its domestic operations last year.
